title: Divide Array Into Equal Pairs
spaceBreakdown:
- int cnt[501]: fixed 501 ints, independent of input size → O(1)
- recursion depth: none
- not counted: input vector, returned bool
approach: Count how many times each value appears. A value can be fully paired up if and only if its count is even. Since values are bounded in [1, 500], use a fixed-size frequency array of 501 ints. After counting, scan all buckets; if any count is odd, return false, otherwise true. This is correct because pairing is purely local to each distinct value-elements of different values can never form a valid pair.
hints: For a fixed value x, what must be true about how many times x appears in nums for all copies of x to be pairable among themselves? The constraints say every nums[i] is between 1 and 500.
Use a frequency array of size 501 (values are 1..500). For nums = [3,2,3,2,2,2], the counts are 2→4 and 3→2; both even, so return true.

**Smallest input** - n = 1, exactly one pair must be formed
`Input: nums = [1,1]` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: returning false whenever `nums.size() == 2` without checking values → returns false

**All equal** - every element is the same value
`Input: nums = [5,5,5,5]` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: checking `cnt[i] == 2` instead of `cnt[i] % 2 == 0` → returns false (count is 4)

**One odd count** - a single value appears an odd number of times
`Input: nums = [1,2,2,3,3,3]` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: returning true upon finding the first even count (sees 2→2) → returns true

**Boundary value 500** - the maximum allowed value appears
`Input: nums = [500,500]` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: declaring `cnt[500]` instead of `cnt[501]` → out-of-bounds write at index 500

followUps.q: Values can be up to 10^9 instead of 500. How does the solution change?
followUps.a: Replace the fixed-size count array with a hash map keyed by value. TC stays O(n); SC becomes O(n) in the worst case where all values are distinct.

followUps.q: Return the actual n pairs instead of just true/false.
followUps.a: Sort the array, then pair adjacent elements at indices (0,1), (2,3), …. If any adjacent pair differs, return empty. TC O(n log n), SC O(n) for the output pairs.

followUps.q: nums arrives as a streaming input of unknown length; you may only store counts for distinct values seen so far.
followUps.a: Maintain a hash map of counts, incrementing per element. Once the stream ends, verify every count is even. TC O(n), SC O(k) where k is the number of distinct values.
